description:
🚀 Team ExoByte Squad | Jump Into Mars

We’re ExoByte Squad, a team passionate about space exploration, game design, and innovative problem-solving. We’re working on Jump Into Mars, a Space Mission Design Game that brings creativity and space science together to make Mars exploration an exciting experience.
summary:
Core Gameplay & Features
Exploration & Discovery: You pilot a rover across a 3D Martian landscape to collect geological samples and capture surface photography.

Environmental Survival: You must manage your rover's battery through daytime solar charging cycles while navigating terrain and balancing energy consumption.

Dynamic Hazards: Sudden Martian dust storms trigger emergency storm closures, forcing you to react quickly and manage resources to survive.

Technical Architecture
3D Engine & Assets: Built with Three.js and custom .glb 3D models to render the rover and Martian terrain directly in the browser.

Development & Deployment: Prototyped using Bolt.new and Lovable, and deployed on Firebase Hosting for instant web access without requiring downloads.
details:
Explore Mars is a browser-based 3D rover survival game designed to bring planetary science directly into an interactive web environment. Building a console-grade 3D graphical interface inside a standard web browser pushes WebGL rendering and memory limits to the edge, making smooth performance without local downloads a major technical feat.

Pushing Web-Based 3D Graphics to the Limit

  • Browser-Native 3D Engine: Running complex 3D terrain, real-time lighting, dust storm particle effects, and physics inside a web browser usually hits severe frame-rate bottlenecks. Using Three.js and optimized custom .glb assets, the game renders a responsive Martian landscape at playable frame rates with zero installation required.
  • Interactive Survival Systems: You control the rover across rugged terrain while monitoring telemetry on a live graphical HUD. Gameplay centers on daytime solar charging cycles, energy management, sample collection, surface photography, and emergency storm closures when dust storms hit.
  • Cloud Deployment: Engineered using modern web workflows (Bolt.new, Lovable) and hosted on Firebase Hosting, allowing anyone on desktop or mobile to launch a heavy 3D planetary simulation instantly via a single URL.

NASA Open Data & Resources Used

  • NASA 3D Resources (nasa3d.arc.nasa.gov / NASA Science): Used official Mars rover geometry and surface reference models to inspire and structure the custom .glb 3D rover assets.
  • NASA Mars Rover Photos & Open Data Portal (data.nasa.gov): Referenced real surface imagery from the Curiosity and Perseverance missions to design accurate terrain textures, rock formations, and photography objectives.
  • NASA Mars Exploration Telemetry & Environmental Data: Modeled the game's solar charging mechanics, battery drain rates, and sudden dust storm hazards around real Martian atmospheric and solar irradiance conditions documented by NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS).
